questions.question: What will be the sum of number of days in the month of January, April, February and November in the year 2000?
questions.solution:
The given year is **2000**.

To determine if **2000** is a leap year, we divide it by 400:

2000 ÷ 400 = 5

Since **2000** is perfectly divisible by 400, it is a **leap year**. Therefore, **February** in the year **2000** had **29 days**.

Now, let us list the number of days for the months mentioned in the question:

 
• Number of days in **January** = 31
 
• Number of days in **April** = 30
 
• Number of days in **February** (Leap Year) = 29
 
• Number of days in **November** = 30

Total sum of days = 31 + 30 + 29 + 30

Total sum = 120

Hence, the sum of the number of days in these months is **120**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **120**.

questions.question: If 19 April 2013 was Friday, then what day was it on 19 September 2013?
questions.solution:
Given reference date is **19 April 2013**, which was a **Friday**.

We need to find the day on **19 September 2013**.

Number of days between 19 April and 19 September in the year 2013:

 
• **April:** 30 − 19 = 11 days
 
• **May:** 31 days
 
• **June:** 30 days
 
• **July:** 31 days
 
• **August:** 31 days
 
• **September:** 19 days (up to the target date)

**Total days** = 11 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 31 + 19 = **153 days**

Now, calculate the **odd days** by dividing the total days by 7:

153 ÷ 7 = 21 weeks and **6 odd days** (as 153 = 21 × 7 + 6)

Now, add the number of odd days to the given day:

**Friday + 6 days = Thursday**

Alternatively, adding 6 days is the same as subtracting 1 day (7 − 1 = 6):

Friday − 1 day = **Thursday**

Hence, the day on **19 September 2013** was **Thursday**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Thursday**.

questions.question: The term of office of the Attorney General of India is
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Not fixed by the constitution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 76** of the **Indian Constitution** establishes the office of the **Attorney General of India** (AGI), who serves as the highest law officer in the country.
 
• The **Constitution of India** does not provide a fixed **tenure** or **term of office** (such as 5 or 6 years) for the Attorney General.
 
• The AGI is appointed by the **President of India** and holds office during the **pleasure of the President**, which means they can be removed at any time without a specific process.
 
• There are no specific **grounds for removal** mentioned in the Constitution for the AGI, unlike the procedure for judges of the **Supreme Court**.
 
• Conventionally, the Attorney General resigns when the **Council of Ministers** (the Government) resigns or is replaced, as the appointment is made based on the advice of the **Union Cabinet**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Qualifications and Appointment**:

 
 
• To be appointed as AGI, a person must be qualified to be appointed as a **Judge of the Supreme Court**.
 
• This requires being a **Citizen of India** and having served as a **High Court Judge** for at least 5 years or as an **Advocate of a High Court** for 10 years.
 
 
 
• **Functions and Rights**:
 
 
• The AGI provides **legal advice** to the **Government of India** on matters referred by the President.
 
• Under **Article 88**, the AGI has the right to speak and participate in the proceedings of both **Houses of Parliament** (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) but does **not have the right to vote**.
 
• They have the **right of audience** in all courts across the territory of India while performing official duties.
 
 
 
• **Remuneration**:
 
 
• The **remuneration** of the AGI is not fixed by the Constitution; it is determined by the **President of India**.

questions.question: On which festival day of Rongali Bihu do people traditionally visit relatives and exchange gifts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kutum Bihu**__.

__
 
• **Rongali Bihu**, also known as **Bohag Bihu**, is the most prominent festival celebrated in **Assam**, marking the beginning of the **Assamese New Year** and the arrival of the spring season.
 
• The festival spans seven days, known as **Xaat Bihu**, and is deeply rooted in the agrarian culture of the state, celebrating the onset of the seeding time.
 
• **Kutum Bihu** is traditionally observed as the **third day** of the festival sequence. The term **Kutum** in the Assamese language signifies **relatives** or **kinfolk**.
 
• On this day, people focus on maintaining social ties by visiting the homes of their **extended families**, **in-laws**, and **close friends**.
 
• The core tradition involves the exchange of **gifts** and hosting elaborate meals, where traditional delicacies like **Jolpan**, **Pitha**, and **Laroo** are served to guests.
 
• This phase of the festival serves to strengthen **communal harmony** and familial bonds after the personal and spiritual rituals of the preceding days.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Goru Bihu**:

 
 
• Observed on the last day of the outgoing year (Sankranti), it is dedicated to the **worship of cattle**.
 
• Cows are washed with **Maha-Haladhi** (turmeric and black gram) and stroked with sprigs of **Dighaloti** and **Makhioti** plants for protection.
 
 
 
• **Manuh Bihu**:
 
 
• The first day of the **New Year**, where people take ceremonial baths and seek blessings from **elders**.
 
• It is characterized by the presentation of the **Bihuwan** (the traditional **Gamosa**) as a token of high esteem and affection.
 
 
 
• **Bohagi Bihu**:
 
 
• This is a general nomenclature for the entire spring festival, often used interchangeably with **Rongali Bihu** to denote the month-long festivities of **dance** and **folk music**.

questions.question: The small intestine receives digestive secretions from which two organs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Liver and pancreas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **small intestine**, specifically the **duodenum**, is the primary site for the chemical digestion of food. It receives vital digestive juices from two major accessory glands: the **liver** and the **pancreas**.
 
• The **liver** secretes **bile juice**, which reaches the duodenum through the **common bile duct**. Bile contains no enzymes but is essential for the **emulsification of fats**, breaking down large fat globules into smaller micelles to increase the surface area for enzyme action.
 
• The **pancreas** functions as a major secretory organ that produces **pancreatic juice**. This juice contains crucial enzymes such as **trypsinogen**, **chymotrypsinogen**, **amylases**, **lipases**, and **nucleases**, which are necessary for digesting proteins, carbohydrates, and fats.
 
• Both the bile duct and the pancreatic duct join together to form the **common hepatopancreatic duct**, which opens into the duodenum, guarded by the **sphincter of Oddi**.
 
• The secretions from these organs are highly alkaline, helping to neutralize the acidic **chyme** received from the stomach, creating an optimal **pH (around 7.8)** for intestinal enzymes to function.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Liver**

 
 
• It is the **largest gland** in the human body, weighing approximately **1.2 to 1.5 kg** in an adult.
 
• Beyond digestion, it performs functions like **detoxification**, **protein synthesis**, and the storage of **glycogen**, **Vitamin A**, and **Vitamin D**.
 
 
 
• **Pancreas**
 
 
• It is a **heterocrine gland**, meaning it has both exocrine functions (secreting digestive enzymes) and endocrine functions (secreting hormones like **insulin** and **glucagon**).
 
• The endocrine part consists of the **Islets of Langerhans**, which regulate blood sugar levels.
 
 
 
• **Excluded Organs**
 
 
• **Kidneys**: Part of the **urinary system**, responsible for filtering blood and removing nitrogenous wastes like **urea**.
 
• **Spleen**: A lymphatic organ that acts as a reservoir for **erythrocytes** (RBCs) and filters the blood for the immune system.
 
• **Lungs**: Central organs of the **respiratory system** designed for the exchange of **oxygen** and **carbon dioxide**.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a component of xylem tissue in plants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Companion cells**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Xylem** is a complex permanent tissue in vascular plants primarily responsible for the **conduction of water and minerals** from the roots to the aerial parts of the plant.
 
• The xylem tissue is composed of four distinct types of cells: **Tracheids**, **Vessels** (or tracheae), **Xylem parenchyma**, and **Xylem fibers**.
 
• **Tracheids** and **Vessels** are the main water-conducting elements; they are dead at maturity and possess thick, **lignified cell walls** to withstand high internal pressure.
 
• **Xylem parenchyma** is the only **living component** of the xylem tissue, primarily functioning in the storage of food materials (starch) and the lateral conduction of water.
 
• **Companion cells** are specialized **parenchymatous cells** that are thin-walled and contain dense cytoplasm and a prominent nucleus.
 
• Unlike the components of the xylem, **Companion cells** are fundamentally associated with **Sieve tube elements** within the **Phloem** tissue, which is responsible for the translocation of organic nutrients.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phloem Tissue Components**:

 
 
• **Sieve Tubes**: Long, tube-like structures that lack a nucleus at maturity and transport **photosynthates**.
 
• **Companion Cells**: Regulate the metabolic activities of sieve tubes and help maintain the **pressure gradient** required for nutrient transport.
 
• **Phloem Parenchyma**: Living cells that store resins, latex, and mucilage.
 
• **Phloem Fibers**: Also known as **bast fibers**, these are dead sclerenchymatous cells providing mechanical strength.
 
 
 
• **Functional Differences**:
 
 
• **Xylem transport** is generally **unidirectional** (upward movement).
 
• **Phloem transport** is **bidirectional**, moving sugars from leaves (source) to storage organs or growing parts (sink).

questions.question: The Law of Octaves was applicable only up to which of the following elements?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1866**, the English scientist **John Newlands** arranged the then-known **56 elements** in increasing order of their **atomic masses**.
 
• He observed that the chemical and physical properties of every **eighth element** were a repetition of the properties of the **first element**, similar to the notes in a musical octave.
 
• This classification, known as **Newlands Law of Octaves**, was found to be applicable and valid only up to **Calcium** (atomic number 20).
 
• For elements heavier than **Calcium**, the periodicity of properties broke down, as every eighth element no longer matched the properties of the first element in the vertical column.
 
• The law worked well only with **lighter elements** and failed to account for the transitional behavior of heavier elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Limitations of Newlands Law**:

 
 
• **Limited Scope**: Newlands assumed only **56 elements** existed in nature and that no more would be discovered, which was later proven wrong.
 
• **Incorrect Grouping**: In an attempt to fit elements into his table, he placed dissimilar elements like **Cobalt** and **Nickel** in the same column as halogens like **Fluorine** and **Chlorine**.
 
• **Noble Gases**: The discovery of **Noble Gases** (He, Ne, Ar) later made the law irrelevant because the eighth element was no longer the one with similar properties.
 
 
 
• **Thorium**:
 
 
• It was the **56th** and final element in Newlands periodic table.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen**:
 
 
• It was the first element in the arrangement due to its lowest **atomic mass**.
 
 
 
• **Potassium**:
 
 
• While **Potassium** is an alkali metal that follows the octave rule relative to **Sodium**, the overall systematic application of the law ceased immediately after **Calcium**.

questions.question: In the context of Earth Structure, which of the following discontinuity divides the crust and mantle?

• The **Mohorovicic discontinuity**, colloquially known as the **Moho**, is the boundary layer that separates the **Earth's crust** from the underlying **mantle**.
 
• It was identified in **1909** by **Andrija Mohorovicic**, a Croatian seismologist, who observed that **seismic waves** accelerated upon reaching this depth due to a change in rock density.
 
• The **Moho** lies at an average depth of **8 kilometers** beneath the ocean floor and roughly **32 to 70 kilometers** beneath **continental landmasses**, particularly under high mountain ranges.
 
• This transition represents a major chemical and rheological shift, moving from the **silica-rich** rocks of the crust to the **peridotite-rich** materials of the **upper mantle**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Conrad Discontinuity**:

 
 
• It acts as the transition zone between the **upper continental crust** (granitic layer) and the **lower continental crust** (basaltic layer).
 
• It is not as globally persistent as the **Moho** and is primarily detected in **continental lithosphere**.
 
 
 
• **Repetti Discontinuity**:
 
 
• This boundary separates the **upper mantle** from the **lower mantle** (mesosphere).
 
• It is typically located at a depth of approximately **660 kilometers** and is characterized by phase changes in **silicate minerals**.
 
 
 
• **Gutenberg Discontinuity**:
 
 
• It defines the interface between the **mantle** and the **outer core**.
 
• Located at a depth of about **2,900 kilometers**, it marks the point where **S-waves** disappear and **P-waves** slow down significantly due to the liquid nature of the **outer core**.
 
 
 
• **Lehmann Discontinuity**:
 
 
• This is the boundary between the **liquid outer core** and the **solid inner core**.
 
• It occurs at a depth of about **5,150 kilometers** below the **Earth's surface**.

questions.question: _______ protects the crop from both frost and hot air currents.

• **Irrigation** is the process of supplying **water** to crops at regular intervals, which is vital for protecting them from extreme weather conditions like **frost** and **hot air currents**.
 
• **Water** has a high **specific heat capacity**, which allows it to absorb and store a large amount of **thermal energy** during the day and release it slowly at night, preventing the **soil temperature** from dropping to dangerous levels during **frost**.
 
• In the presence of **hot air currents** or **Loo**, water is absorbed by the roots and moves through the plant to the leaves, where it evaporates in a process called **transpiration**.
 
• The evaporation of water from the **stomata** creates a **cooling effect** on the plant surface, much like sweating in humans, which prevents the **protoplasm** from drying out and protects **plant tissues** from **desiccation**.
 
• Maintaining adequate **soil moisture** through **irrigation** ensures that the plant remains **turgid**, allowing it to withstand the physical stress caused by strong, dry winds.

• It is an **organic substance** obtained from the decomposition of **plant or animal wastes** by microbes.
 
• It improves **soil texture** and **water-holding capacity** but does not directly provide **thermal insulation** against frost.

For any four numbers a, b, c, and d in proportion (a : b :: c : d), the relation **a × d = b × c** always holds true.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence where the homonym "watch" means a timepiece.

options.text: The guard will watch over the prisoners.
I bought a new wrist watch yesterday.
Watch your step on the slippery road.
They went to watch the football match.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**I bought a new wrist watch yesterday.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• A **homonym** is a word that shares the same spelling and pronunciation as another word but has a completely different meaning. The word **watch** is a prominent example in English linguistics, functioning as both a **noun** and a **verb**.

• When used as a **noun**, specifically in the context of a **timepiece**, it refers to a small, **portable instrument** for measuring and showing time, typically worn on a strap around the **wrist** or carried in a pocket.

• In the sentence 'I bought a new wrist watch yesterday.', the word **watch** is preceded by the modifier **wrist** and the article 'a', identifying it as a **countable noun** representing a physical object.

• The word evolved from the Old English **wæccan**, which originally meant 'to be awake' or 'to remain alert'. Historically, the term shifted from the act of **surveillance** (a watchman) to the period of duty (a watch), and eventually to the **mechanical device** used to track those shifts in the 15th and 16th centuries.

• The presence of the word **wrist** in this sentence serves as a **semantic marker**, eliminating ambiguity and confirming the **timepiece** definition.

 **Additional Information__**

• The term **watch** as a **verb** carries several distinct meanings based on **contextual usage**:

• **Visual Observation**: To look at or observe something with **sustained attention** over a duration, such as a **football match** or a television program.

• **Surveillance and Guarding**: To keep a person, group, or place under **protective** or **restrictive supervision** (e.g., a guard monitoring prisoners).

• **Vigilance**: To be **cautious** or alert to potential hazards, often used in **imperative sentences** like 'Watch your step'.

• **Monitoring**: To follow the **progress** or development of a situation closely to detect changes.

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
Are the children preparing a play for the school annual day?

options.text: Has a play been prepared by the children for the school annual day?
Was a play prepared by the children for the school annual day?
Is a play prepared by the children for the school annual day?
Is a play being prepared by the children for the school annual day?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Is a play being prepared by the children for the school annual day?**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The sentence provided is in the **Present Continuous Tense** and follows an **Interrogative Structure**. In **Active Voice**, this structure is: **Is/Am/Are + Subject + Verb-ing + Object?**

• To convert a **Present Continuous** sentence into **Passive Voice**, the structure must be: **Is/Am/Are + New Subject (Object of the active voice) + being + Past Participle (V3) + by + New Object (Subject of the active voice)?**

• The **Object** in the active sentence is **'a play'**. Since **'a play'** is a **singular noun**, the passive sentence begins with the auxiliary verb **'Is'** to maintain grammatical agreement.

• The **Subject** of the active sentence, **'the children'**, becomes the **Agent** in the passive sentence and is preceded by the preposition **'by'**.

• The verb **'preparing'** is transformed into its **Passive** form by using the auxiliary **'being'** (to indicate continuous action) followed by the **Past Participle** form **'prepared'**.

• The phrase **'for the school annual day'** acts as an **Adverbial Complement** and remains unchanged in its relative position within the sentence.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Rules for Voice Change in Interrogative Sentences:**

• **Tense Consistency:** The **Tense** of the sentence must never change during the conversion from active to passive voice.

• **Sentence Type:** An **Interrogative** sentence in the active voice must remain **Interrogative** in the passive voice.

• **Pronoun Changes:** While not applicable here, subjects like **'I'**, **'He'**, or **'They'** would change to **'me'**, **'him'**, or **'them'** respectively when moved to the object position.

• **Present Simple Passive:** Uses **Is/Am/Are + V3** (e.g., **'Is a play prepared...?'**).

• **Past Continuous Passive:** Uses **Was/Were + being + V3** (e.g., **'Was a play being prepared...?'**).

</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?
The broken bridge had been repaired by the villagers before the storm struck.

options.text: The villagers repaired the broken bridge before the storm struck.
The villagers repair the broken bridge before the storm struck.
The villagers had repaired the broken bridge before the storm struck.
The storm struck after the villagers repaired the broken bridge.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The villagers had repaired the broken bridge before the storm struck.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• To convert a sentence from **Passive Voice** to **Active Voice**, the **agent** of the action (the villagers) must be shifted to the **subject** position at the beginning of the sentence.
 
• The original sentence is in the **Past Perfect Tense** in the passive form, identified by the auxiliary structure **had been + past participle** (had been repaired).
 
• In the **Active Voice**, the **Past Perfect Tense** must maintain its temporal aspect by using the structure **had + past participle** (had repaired) without the word **been**.
 
• The **passive subject** (The broken bridge) becomes the **direct object** in the active sentence, following the main verb.
 
• The **adverbial clause** (before the storm struck) remains constant to indicate the sequence of events, where one past action was completed before another past action occurred.
 
• The resulting active construction follows the **Subject + Verb + Object** pattern: **The villagers** (Subject) + **had repaired** (Verb) + **the broken bridge** (Object).

 **Additional Information__**

 
• Understanding **Tense Consistency** in Voice Conversion:
 
 
• **Simple Past Tense**: Option 1 uses **repaired**, which fails to capture the **Past Perfect** necessity of the original sentence indicating an action completed prior to the storm.
 
• **Simple Present Tense**: Option 2 uses **repair**, which is grammatically incorrect in a context describing a past event (the storm struck).
 
• **Syntactic Reordering**: Option 4 changes the **focus** and **conjunction** structure, which alters the original meaning and emphasis of the source sentence.
 
• **Past Perfect Active Rule**: This tense is specifically used to clarify that the **repair** work was finished before the **storm** arrived, maintaining the logical timeline.
 
 
</ul

questions.solution: इसका सही उत्तर **'सुरक्षा'** है। **__Key Points__** **गद्यांश के अनुसार**, __ • गद्यांश का मुख्य विषय **भीड़ नियंत्रण** व्यवस्था है, जिसका सीधा संबंध सार्वजनिक स्थानों पर लोगों की **सुरक्षा** सुनिश्चित करने से है। • इसमें **भगदड़** और **दुर्घटनाओं** को रोकने की प्रभावशीलता पर जोर दिया गया है, जो कि **सुरक्षा प्रबंधन** के मुख्य भाग हैं। • आयोजनों को **सुरक्षित** रूप से संपन्न कराना ही इस व्यवस्था का मूल लक्ष्य बताया गया है। • इसलिए, यह गद्यांश **सुरक्षा व्यवस्था** पर केंद्रित है। **Additional Information__** **अन्य विकल्पों का विश्लेषण:** **प्रशासनिक** - __ • इसका संबंध **शासन** और **कार्यालयी प्रबंधन** से है। यद्यपि सुरक्षा प्रशासन का एक हिस्सा हो सकती है, लेकिन गद्यांश का प्राथमिक केंद्र विशेष रूप से सुरक्षा है। **आर्थिक** - • यह **धन**, **बजट** या **वित्त** से जुड़ी व्यवस्था है, जिसकी चर्चा इस गद्यांश में नहीं की गई है। **शैक्षिक** - • यह **शिक्षा** और **पठन-पाठन** की प्रक्रिया से संबंधित है, जो यहाँ के संदर्भ में प्रासंगिक नहीं है। 216:Td19, इसका सही उत्तर '**नियंत्रण और सुरक्षा'** है। **Key Points__** **गद्यांश के अनुसार **, • भीड़ नियंत्रण व्यवस्था का मुख्य और प्राथमिक उद्देश्य किसी भी बड़े आयोजन के दौरान उचित **नियंत्रण और सुरक्षा** सुनिश्चित करना है। • यह व्यवस्था इसलिए की जाती है ताकि **भीड़** को अनुशासित रखा जा सके और किसी भी प्रकार की **अनहोनी** से बचा जा सके। • गद्यांश स्पष्ट करता है कि सही प्रबंधन से जीवन की रक्षा होती है, अतः **नियंत्रण और सुरक्षा** ही इसका मूल ध्येय है।

questions.question: भीड़ नियंत्रण का मुख्य उद्देश्य क्या है?
questions.solution:
इसका सही उत्तर '**नियंत्रण और सुरक्षा'** है। 

**__Key Points__**

**गद्यांश के अनुसार **,

__
 
• भीड़ नियंत्रण व्यवस्था का मुख्य और प्राथमिक उद्देश्य किसी भी बड़े आयोजन के दौरान उचित **नियंत्रण और सुरक्षा** सुनिश्चित करना है।
 
• यह व्यवस्था इसलिए की जाती है ताकि **भीड़** को अनुशासित रखा जा सके और किसी भी प्रकार की **अनहोनी** से बचा जा सके।
 
• गद्यांश स्पष्ट करता है कि सही प्रबंधन से जीवन की रक्षा होती है, अतः **नियंत्रण और सुरक्षा** ही इसका मूल ध्येय है।

**Additional Information__** **अन्य विकल्प:**

**मनोरंजन** - 

 
• यह आयोजनों का एक हिस्सा हो सकता है, लेकिन भीड़ नियंत्रण का उद्देश्य मनोरंजन करना नहीं, बल्कि लोगों को सुरक्षित रखना है।

**व्यापार** - 

 
• भीड़ नियंत्रण एक सुरक्षात्मक प्रक्रिया है, इसका सीधा संबंध आर्थिक या व्यापारिक लाभ से नहीं होता है।

**प्रचार** -
